A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EquiBench and retain matching benchmark construction and experiments. The main text, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing substantive changes to be distinguished from relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 17 LLMs, prompting experiments, prediction-bias measurements and CUDA case studies, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports evaluations of 19 LLMs and a new syntactic-similarity analysis, alongside the retained prompting, bias and case-study results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same DCE, CUDA scheduling, superoptimization and contest-submission/variable-renaming construction procedures. The newly disclosed LLVM tool size does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 2,400-pair benchmark across four languages and six equivalence categories, with identical Table 1 statistics and data sources. The similarity analysis examines retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Claude 3.7 Sonnet and o4-mini while retaining all 17 earlier models and the random baseline. Comparator membership in the prompting and bias comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 Section 5.2 introduces Moss-based syntactic-similarity measurement and examines its relationship with accuracy separately for equivalent and inequivalent pairs. The existing dataset balance, accuracy metric and four prompting configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a diagnostic analysis testing whether predictions track syntactic similarity. Earlier scaling, transformation-difficulty, prompting, bias and synchronization-bug analyses remain; the bias discussion and case studies move to Appendices A.1 and A.2.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports statistical testing of similarity–accuracy trends at alpha = 0.05. It does not specify the test or provide p-values, and adds no repeated-run or seed information.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds Claude 3.7 Sonnet at 67.0% overall and o4-mini at 82.3%, making o4-mini the leader over the retained o3-mini result of 78.0%. Aggregate means change, but all original model rows, prompting scores and bias results remain unchanged. Section 5.2 newly reports increasing accuracy with similarity for equivalent pairs and decreasing accuracy for inequivalent pairs.

T1.justification: The category-specific equivalence definitions in Sections 3.1–3.4 remain unchanged. New discussion of soundness and reasoning-trace verification introduces no formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The benchmark and automated-generation contributions remain intact. v2 adds reliance on syntactic similarity rather than robust semantic understanding as an explicit abstract, introduction and conclusion finding, extending v1's claims about difficulty and inequivalence bias.

C2.justification: Sections 5.2 and 6 substantially expand interpretation: similarity dependence motivates harder benchmark pairs and execution-trace training, while new discussion addresses labeling guarantees and the difficulty of validating reasoning beyond binary answers. The original label-noise limitation and CUDA case interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix A.1 supplies detailed few-shot/CoT examples; v2 Appendix A.4 retains only zero-shot templates. v2 also removes Together AI/API access, default-temperature and GPT-4o parsing/random-fallback disclosures from Section 4. It adds LLVM implementation-size information, but substantially reduces documentation needed to reproduce retained experiments.

R1.justification: The introduction and new Section 6 substantially broaden positioning to meaning versus form, code-generation and clone-detection tasks, and labeling guarantees relative to random-testing/refactoring approaches. Added citations include Bender and Koller, DCE-LLM and Moss; several original model-report citations disappear. The existing EQBENCH/SeqCoBench comparison remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around execution semantics. Results gain a Difficulty Analysis section and a new Discussion and Future Directions section; bias and case studies move into reorganized appendices, and prompt documentation is substantially shortened. The title, author block and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a small equivalence example to a full-width pipeline overview. Figure 5 and the scaling plot relocate; Table 4 becomes appendix Table A1, and the full bias table gains the Table A2 caption. Most graphics and the basic document layout remain intact.

improvement.justification: The additional model comparisons and expanded discussion are useful, but v2 removes detailed prompts and serving/output-parsing information for retained experiments. Its new central similarity finding supplies alpha = 0.05 without a specified test, effect sizes or supporting numerical breakdown. The evidential value of that addition cannot be assessed sufficiently to weigh reliably against the concrete reproducibility losses.
